scale.interpretation: observed/self-reported distress estimate; not a diagnosis or validated clinical instrument

levels.label: low
levels.description: Little current distress; able to reflect and engage.

levels.label: mild
levels.description: Noticeable worry or tension with generally preserved functioning.

levels.label: moderate
levels.description: Distress interferes with concentration or decisions; support and clarification may help.

levels.label: high
levels.description: Strong distress, narrowed attention, or marked avoidance; prioritize pacing, validation, and safety assessment where indicated.

levels.label: very_high
levels.description: Overwhelming distress or inability to function in the moment; assess immediate safety and urgent support needs rather than assuming routine counselling is sufficient.

scoring_guidance: Do not infer a numeric anxiety score from writing style alone.
Prefer an explicit client self-rating when available.
Record the evidence and uncertainty behind each score.
A score is not a diagnosis, risk assessment, or substitute for a qualified clinician.
Do not force scores to decline; realistic sessions may remain stable or fluctuate.
source: Project-defined operational rubric; not represented as a scale authored or validated by Beck or Rogers.
